From: Krista Nguyen <krista@finovate.com>

Date: Thu, 30 Apr 2026 09:12:05 -0700
Subject: Live chat delay noticed — tokens arriving in bursts

Hi Olga,

We started seeing the live chat responses from Redwood for our customer-facing widget slow down around 08:55 PT — replies are coming in long bursts instead of a steady stream. This makes the typing indicator and progress bar spike and customers are seeing 3–8s pauses between chunks.

Can you confirm whether this looks like a client-side socket drop, or if it might be on Redwood's streaming path? We haven't changed our deployment. We captured a short HAR and a couple of sample request IDs: req_83af2 and req_83af9.

We have a call at 11:00 PT but wanted to flag this now — it's affecting checkout flows.

Thanks,
Krista

Hi Krista — thanks for the heads up and the HAR + request IDs. We're seeing elevated token emission latency on the streaming shard that serves your region; eng is triaging now.

Short-term we recommend two quick client-side mitigations while we investigate:
- Enable non-blocking partial renders: treat each chunk as deliverable even if smaller than usual.
- If possible, switch this route to the non-streaming (single-response) endpoint for the peak window — that reduces the backpressure we see today.

We're attaching a short emergency runbook with concrete steps we can coordinate (see attachment: streaming-bridging-runbook.pdf). Marcus will lead the telemetry/data pull and Rishi will coordinate the quick config change if needed.

I'll update in ~30 mins with initial findings and an ETA for a permanent fix.

—Olga

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Apr 2026 10:05:10 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Live chat delay — initial telemetry

Forwarding the initial traces I pulled; summary below.

Summary: between 08:50–09:05 PT we observed an increase in tail latency for token emission on the streaming shard servicing Finovate due to an interaction between prefix-KV cache eviction and a scheduled background compaction job. When compaction overlapped with high concurrency, per-token kernel dispatch latency rose from ~12ms to ~80–120ms for a subset of sessions.

Temporary server-side mitigations I'm deploying now (will keep you posted):
- Pause background compaction on affected hosts for the next 45 minutes.
- Reduce default chunk size emitted by runtime from 16 tokens -> 8 tokens for the Finovate routing policy (low-risk, reduces emit serialization windows).
- Set connection keepalive to 90s for long-polling websockets to reduce handshake churn.

I also included quick client fallback guidance you can share with Krista in the notification:
- Decrease client streaming buffer threshold to 6 tokens so UI renders earlier.
- If you rely on final-confidence heuristics, add a 1s debounce before showing final state to avoid flicker during retries.

I'll attach the event ids to the runbook for the postmortem.

-Marcus

Date: Thu, 30 Apr 2026 11:02:47 -0700
Subject: Update: temporary mitigations in place — please try fallback

Hi Krista,

Update from eng: we've applied the temporary server-side mitigations (paused compaction on the affected hosts and reduced emission chunk size). Can you try the following immediate client change and let us know if you still see bursts?

Client quick-change (safe, reversible):
1) Set streamChunkThreshold = 6 (previously 12) so your UI renders smaller chunks immediately.
2) If using the websocket client, enable simple retry-with-jitter for 502/504 (max 2 retries).
3) Optional: for mission-critical flows (checkout), switch to the non-streaming endpoint for the next 90 minutes by setting routeOverride: 'non-stream' — we'll keep traffic shaping to avoid capacity issues.

Example config snippet you can paste into your frontend router:
// Finovate sample fallback config
{
  streaming: { chunkThreshold: 6, maxRetries: 2 },
  routeOverride: 'non-stream' // use only if checkout is impacted
}

We've also provisioned extra capacity on the edge for your routing policy and are monitoring. Attached runbook includes step-by-step verification and the exact event ids we saw. If you confirm the workaround helps, we'll prepare a short postmortem and a proposal for a targeted firmware/serving runtime patch in the next 72 hours.

Thanks — appreciate the quick signal.

Olga
